newsitem.title: CHINA: China Industrial Bank gets new governor.
newsitem.headline: China Industrial Bank gets new governor.

text.p: The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) has appointed a new president following the retirement of former bank chief Zhang Xiao, officials said on Monday.
Liu Tinghuan, 55, a former vice-president of the ICBC, was appointed as president last December, a bank official told Reuters by telephone. His appointment had not been announced.
Zhang left the post after reaching the official retirement age of 60, the official said.
The new bank president had pledged to steer the bank on a path of stable and healthy development by adopting a package of reforms in 1997, the Financial News said.
"Competition in the financial sector is growing fiercer day by day...(so) we must seek greater development through stable and healthy operation," the newspaper quoted Liu as saying.

The bank would reform its accounting and auditing systems and strengthen management of foreign exchange, Liu said but gave no details. Loans would be granted on the basis of an enterprise's performance and market potential, he said.
The bank would also support growth in the housing industry by developing individual loans and strictly banning loans for office buildings and luxury villas and hotels, he said.
